newsitem.title: USA: Ex-worker sues NY Times, cites religion.
newsitem.headline: Ex-worker sues NY Times, cites religion.

text.p: A former office worker at the New York Times Co sued the newspaper company on Thursday, charging that as a Jew she was the victim of religious discrimination.
Miriam Humbach of Manhattan, who was employed in the flagship newspaper's circulation department from January, 1987 to August 1995, said she was ultimately fired "on the basis of her sex."
A N.Y. Times spokeswoman said the company has not seen the lawsuit, so it could not comment.

Humbach claimed in the suit she was required by her boss to work overtime on September 15, 1994, the evening of Yom Kippur, the Day of Atonement, the holiest day of the Jewish year, and the following day, the holiday.
She alleged she was also required to work on Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish new year, later that month. She claimed she had scheduled the time off.
She alleged that her boss told her she was "not entitled to special treatment because she is Jewish."
She also alleged that she was terminated out of seniority due to her sex, while two less senior male workers were retained.
